messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for dedicated pool 'eu-central-3' (streaming) — auto-escalation threshold crossed. p95=1.1s p99=28.7s queue_depth=374 warmup_inflight=42

mira: seeing same on the dashboards. streaming stall spikes at ~11:23 UTC. customer-facing SLOs hit. paging now.

alex: are we sure this is pool saturation vs model slowdown? metrics show GPUs at ~98% and handshake/slot-assign latencies climbing.

jordan: stack traces show lots of handshake timeouts between router -> pool-manager. autoscaler reports "scale_request_sent" but nodes not coming ready quickly. possible warmup backlog.

samir: adding logs: ```
# pool-manager
2026-03-15T11:22:58Z INFO scale_request_sent id=sr-9a3f
2026-03-15T11:23:10Z WARN slot_alloc_delay ms=12045 pool=eu-central-3
2026-03-15T11:23:37Z ERROR warmup_timeout model=gpt-open-ggml seq=4096
```

lia: Support reports a customer (acme-corp) experiencing streaming stalls ~20-30s and aborted connections. They've opened a ticket and are asking for ETA.

mira: initial triage: dedicated pool saturated due to a burst from a large customer plus several backlog replay jobs that should've been throttled. autoscaler lagged because our warmup handshake waits for KV sync which is queued.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) enable manual scale +2 nodes to the pool, 2) drop non-critical replay jobs, 3) enable emergency routing to fallback-model (smaller quantized) for streaming flows, 4) reduce batch_max to 1 for affected routes.

jordan: I'm on manual scale now. invoking: ```
$ /ops/pool-scale --pool eu-central-3 --add 2 --reason "latencypulse emergency"
Request submitted -> scale_op=op-324
```

samir: pushing a temporary throttle: set priority_queue for replay jobs to low and cap concurrency 1. ```
PATCH /internal/queues/replay
{ "max_concurrency": 1, "priority": "low" }
```

lia: letting Acme know we're scaling and routing to fallback. sending short status: "We are mitigating a performance issue in eu-central-3. We are adding capacity and routing to a lower-latency fallback model for affected streams. ETA ~8-12 min."

mira: also: enable kv-warmup-bypass for new nodes so they can accept traffic earlier. risk: slightly higher cold-kv misses but reduces handshake time. Need SRE lead ok.

alex: I approve. runbook step 7 permits bypass under emergency. samir, can you flip kv bypass gate?

samir: flipping gate now -> `featuregate.kv_warmup_bypass=on` -> applied to pool-manager config. monitor logs.

incidents-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 18m. mira -> next oncall is alex. mark triage owner.

mira: I'm staying on until steady-state but alex will take over post-handoff. alex, can you own RCA followup?

alex: yep. taking ownership after handoff. currently verifying scale op status.

jordan: scale op op-324 reported nodes provisioning. new nodes entering warmup but accepting connections due to bypass. observed a drop in slot_alloc_delay from ~12s -> 400ms within 90s. p99 falling.

samir: queue_depth down from 374 -> 72 after throttle + scale + bypass. good sign.

lia: Customer updated: Acme sees degraded streams for last 12 minutes but reconnects successful; they asked for root cause once stable.

mira: plan for next 30m: 1) keep bypass on for 10m, 2) let new nodes finish proper KV sync, 3) restore normal replay rates, 4) collect traces for handshake latencies and autoscaler event timeline. we want a timeline of scale_request -> node_ready -> handshake_success.

alex: capturing traces now. pulling autoscaler events: ```
- 11:22:58 scale_request_sent sr-9a3f
- 11:23:05 asg-provision-start nodepool=eu-central-3
- 11:23:45 node-init-complete n=i-0a7
- 11:24:05 handshake_success n=i-0a7
```

jordan: interesting: node-init-complete -> handshake_success gap ~20s for new nodes; but earlier existing nodes had handshake stalls 10-30s. hypothesis: KV sync backlog added variable warmup that autoscaler didn't account for.

samir: for postmortem candidate actions: add warmup-time-slack to autoscaler; make KV sync async with early-accept option (but gated); give replay queue separate throttle budget that doesn't count toward hotshot capacity; add better telemetry: per-request handshake latency histogram.

lia: Customer update: Acme acknowledged message and will wait for official RCA. They asked to be notified when RCA available.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated: partial. p99 dropped to 1.8s; p95 back under 1s. Keep monitoring. Incident severity lowered to sev-2.

mira: leaving incident channel in 10m. Alex will coordinate postmortem and customer write-up. tags: root-cause=dedicated-saturation, contributing=warmup-handshake-delay, mitigation=manual-scale+kv-bypass+replay-throttle.

alex: will open a postmortem ticket and invite eng-runtime, autoscaler, and support. thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

jordan: note for postmortem: include sample request IDs for p99 traces (req-7a2f, req-8c3b). also add graphs for slot_alloc_delay and kv-sync-queue-length.

samir: adding follow-up action: lower default batch_max for streaming routes by 25% during burst windows to reduce hotshot amplification.

lia: I'll keep Acme updated and file the support case link in the PM.

incidents-bot: REMINDER: handoff in 6m. oncall -> alex.

mira: handing off now to alex. thanks team, I'll be on slack if we need me.

alex: taking over. continuing monitoring and starting RCA doc.
